findings.impact: With the default StateRefresh::Request, one scoped PermissionSetCache serves the whole request, while panel_state is a single row per panel (primary key panel only) and StateToken has no tenant. A Grants check in tenant A at revision V stores memo[A]=V and the raw grants under that token. After a committed revoke and touch to V+1, a later check in the same request whose scope tenant differs (another organization, or TenantRef::global()) has its own empty memo, cold-reads V+1, and rememberState records only that second key. The next check for tenant A still uses memo V, PermissionSetCache::get hits the V raw set in request memory or the shared store, and Authorizer::decide Allows the revoked grant with StateToken V.
findings.norm: 09 §8: a request-mode cold load that discovers a newer version advances the request memo and clears old raw entries; the old token must not be issued as a historical snapshot, because the DB API cannot read it. StateToken is storageId, panel, incarnation, version, generation, fingerprint. D15 §4: one current fenced authority revision per consumed route.
findings.correction: Build the request state-memo digest from panel, code fingerprint, cache generation, source, read mode, and authority handle only. Keep tenant solely in PermissionSetCache::key for the raw set. On a cold read whose StateToken differs from the memoized token for that route, replace that one memo and drop the request raw sets before any later check (the existing forgetState/rememberState path once the key is shared). Later contribution keys then use the new token, so entries stored under the superseded token are not reused in that request. A warm hit on an unchanged memo stays one state read and zero grant reads (P10).

future_scope_notes: Reuse of a revision that no cold read in the same request has superseded remains the accepted StateRefresh::Request window (V18 on a new request, P10). Recognized root transactions remain P4.20. Cross-process races, Redis, and replica lag remain P4.21.
